sources.title: Information Technology Act, 2000 (as amended by ITAA 2008, police.py.gov.in)

section_notes.66A: LEGAL STATUS NOTE: Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (punishment for sending offensive messages through communication service) was struck down as unconstitutional by the Supreme Court of India in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, (2015) 5 SCC 1, decided on 24 March 2015. Section 66A is not valid and not enforceable: no one can be prosecuted under it, and it must not be listed as a current cybercrime offence. Some older copies of the Act still print its text.
section_notes.43A: LEGAL STATUS NOTE: Section 43A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (compensation for failure to protect data) remains in force until Section 44(2) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 commences. Under the MeitY commencement notification of 13 November 2025, Section 44(2) commences 18 months after notification, that is in May 2027.

sources.notes: Cyber-relevant sections include 75, 77, 78, 79 (offences against women online), 111-112 (organised/cyber-enabled crime chains). Chunk with section boundaries preserved.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (meity.gov.in, official Gazette PDF)
sources.notes: Phased commencement -- check meity.gov.in/content/digital-personal-data-protection-act-2023 for current commencement status before citing as fully in force.
sources.status_note: LEGAL STATUS NOTE (per MeitY commencement notification of 13 November 2025): the DPDP Act is being brought into force in phases. Sections 1(2), 2, 18-26, 35, 38-43, 44(1) and 44(3) are in force. Consent Manager provisions (section 6(9) and 27(1)(d)) follow after 12 months (November 2026). Most remaining provisions, including sections 3-17 (duties of Data Fiduciaries and rights of Data Principals) and 44(2), come into force 18 months after notification (May 2027). Do not state that these duties are currently enforceable.

sources.status_note: LEGAL STATUS NOTE: The Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026 came into force on 1 July 2026 and repealed the 2021 scheme. Complaints received before 1 July 2026 remain governed by the 2021 scheme. Complaints are lodged online on the RBI CMS portal (cms.rbi.org.in).
